dimensions.reasons: The author final render shared_activity_lounge.png clearly presents the requested single indoor activity area: modular block seating around a low central table and patterned rug, with the striped café kiosk at right, a freestanding CONNECT screen at left, and a hovering drone overhead. The pastel coral, orange, cream, blue, and yellow palette follows the requested illustrated modular language and avoids the reference image's people and collage composition.
issues: The seating reads more as oversized toy-brick/display blocks than as convincingly designed modular lounge seating.
The final scene is visually sparse and toy-like for a residential public shared activity space.
The very bright render weakens several details that should help establish the intended activity-zone design.

dimensions.reasons: In the close author view, the stools, benches, café counter, screen base, table, and rug are generally grounded on the floor, while the drone is deliberately airborne as requested. The café canopy is visibly supported by four slim coral posts.
issues: Group A wide_back.png, wide_left.png, and wide_right.png reveal an incomplete, cutaway-like shell with large open sides, an oversized roof slab, and disconnected parapet strips rather than a coherent enclosed interior.
The rug and colored inset panels appear extremely paper-thin in cam_submitted.png and detail_lounge.png.
Some of the loose block modules look placed as scattered props rather than clearly functioning as stable seats or stools.

dimensions.reasons: shared_activity_lounge.png uses a consistent matte flat-shaded look and closely follows the requested coral pink, orange-yellow, cream-white, vivid blue, and bright-yellow palette. The drone, striped café canopy, graphic screen, studded modules, table, and colored rug motifs are independently recognizable.
issues: The repeated raised studs make nearly all seating components read as LEGO-like bricks, reducing the distinction between seating, stools, and loose play blocks.
The strong washout reduces the apparent contrast between cream, white, and pale pink surfaces.

dimensions.reasons: The scene is coherently assembled in a deliberately simplified illustrative style, and the designated author view has a readable three-quarter composition with no people or unintended reference-image figures.
issues: shared_activity_lounge.png is strongly overexposed, especially across the back wall, café canopy, and floor, producing a hazy low-contrast image.
Soft shadows are so faint that furniture-ground contact and room depth are weakened.
The sparse room and toy-brick forms do not fully sell the setting as a polished residential shared lounge.

dimensions.reasons: The central relationship is clear in shared_activity_lounge.png: two facing/modular bench groups and stools surround the low coffee table on the patterned rug; the screen is placed to the left, the café is on the right, and the drone remains above the activity zone. All required major elements are visible together in the author camera view.
issues: The foreground stools and loose blocks crowd the rug edge and make the central zone feel somewhat cluttered rather than providing clearly defined circulation.
The café counter is relatively close to the seating/rug cluster, leaving limited visible walkway space on that side.
Evaluator wide views expose a large amount of empty exterior base and open shell that does not reinforce the intended continuous interior.

dimensions.reasons: Within shared_activity_lounge.png, the coffee table is appropriately lower than the surrounding benches, the screen has a plausible standing height, and the café canopy is taller than the seating. The drone is small enough to read as a compact hovering device rather than a dominant centerpiece.
issues: Without human-scale cues, the oversized studded cubes can read alternately as stools, small furniture, or toy blocks.
The screen and café canopy are visually large relative to the compact seating area, making the space feel slightly miniature.
The low, broad roof shown in Group A makes the room volume feel compressed and disproportionate from exterior views.

dimensions.reasons: The material treatment is appropriately simple, matte, and consistent across the modules, café frame, rug, screen, and drone. The lighting is generally bright and soft, matching the requested non-dramatic illustrated presentation.
issues: The author final shared_activity_lounge.png has substantial blown highlights and bloom-like washout on the back wall, floor, and canopy.
The lighting makes white and cream materials merge and obscures fine rug and seating details.
The weak shadow definition limits depth despite the otherwise appropriate matte materials.

dimensions.reasons: All principal requested scene elements are present in the author final: colorful modular seating/stools, a central low table, a rug with colored panels, dots and wavy lines, a red/pink-and-white striped café corner, a floor-standing display, and one hovering drone. The display visibly says only “CONNECT,” and the scene contains no people, headset users, cyclists, phones, or extra technological devices.
issues: The requested neutral interior enclosure is only partially realized in the actual scene geometry: Group A shows open room sides and an awkward exterior roof/parapet arrangement.
The distinction between intentionally provided stools and extra loose decorative toy bricks is not always clear.
The rug pattern is present but comparatively minimal and flattened relative to the more graphic patterned language requested.

criteria.criterion: The work must be a newly authored, continuous residential shared-activity interior and the complete Blender scene must obey the prompt's exclusive environment-content boundary.
The complete scene must use the requested reference-derived illustrative treatment, matte material system, palette hierarchy, modular form language, and restrained neutral interior shell.
The central lounge must combine block-built seating and stools with exactly one functionally central low coffee table.
criteria.evidence: The author-final image shared_activity_lounge clearly shows two low coral/orange bench-like seating units made from colored rectangular studded modules, several surrounding cube ottomans/stools, and one low cream-and-white rectangular coffee table placed centrally between them.

criteria.criterion: The colorful rug must visibly carry both required pattern families.
criteria.evidence: In shared_activity_lounge, a large multicolor rectangular floor rug/mat sits beneath the lounge. Its colored panels visibly include blue and coral wavy-line motifs as well as multiple small circular dot motifs.

criteria.criterion: The side coffee corner must be recognizable and include its complete red-and-white striped awning identity.
criteria.evidence: At the right side of shared_activity_lounge, a recognizable counter kiosk has four slim supports and a projecting canopy with clearly alternating coral-red and white stripes.

criteria.criterion: The display must combine the required floor-standing form with exact, exclusive screen content.
criteria.evidence: The single upright display at left in shared_activity_lounge legibly reads “CONNECT,” but the screen also contains a separate coral horizontal line beneath the word, which is an additional visible mark.

criteria.criterion: Exactly one small drone must be recognizable and visibly unsupported overhead.
criteria.evidence: One small blue-and-yellow quadcopter with four visible rotor disks is clearly airborne above the central furniture in shared_activity_lounge, with open space separating it from the ceiling, floor, and kiosk.

criteria.criterion: The complete element arrangement must provide coherent human scale, clear functional relationships, and usable circulation without visible stacking or substantial occlusion.
The single author-final camera must provide the specified elevated three-quarter view with clear, unobstructed, and undistorted visibility of every required physical scene element.
criteria.evidence: The author-final shared_activity_lounge is a single landscape three-quarter interior view from slightly above. It visibly includes the lounge seating/stools, central table, patterned rug, striped kiosk, standing screen, hovering drone, and the neutral room floor, walls, and ceiling without fisheye distortion or principal-object cropping.

criteria.criterion: The original scene lighting and final result must provide bright, even, soft internal illumination without exterior-light dependence or dramatic darkness.
The delivery must contain both a clear high-resolution author-final image and its openable, editable, corresponding Blender project.

notes: The submission successfully includes and visibly arranges every core requested object in a clean stylized palette, with a readable CONNECT screen and no forbidden people or reference-image collage content. Its principal weaknesses are the overexposed final render, overly toy-brick-like seating treatment, crowded rug area, and the incomplete room shell revealed by evaluator multi-views.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
